message.content:
The idea of a single “best” movie is inherently subjective—different people value storytelling, technical craft, cultural impact, and personal taste in different ways. However, several films released in 2020 received widespread critical acclaim, high audience scores, and major award recognition. Below is a short, objective snapshot of some of those standout titles: | Film | Release Year | Key Accolades / Notable Achievements | Why It Stands Out (objective points) | |------|--------------|-------------------------------------|--------------------------------------| | **Nomadland** | 2020 | *Best Picture*, *Best Director* (Chloé Zhao), *Best Actress* (Frances McDormand) – 93rd Academy Awards; 10‑film Oscar nomination; 2020 Golden Globe winner | • 100% Rotten Tomatoes score (critics)
• Strong box‑office performance for a pandemic‑era release
• Praised for its realistic portrayal of modern American nomadism | | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | 2020 | 5‑film Oscar nomination (including Best Picture); 2020 BAFTA nomination | • 95% Rotten Tomatoes score
• Acclaimed for its sharp dialogue and historical relevance | | **Soul** | 2020 | 3‑film Oscar nomination (including Best Animated Feature); 2020 BAFTA win | • 98% Rotten Tomatoes score
• Recognized for its innovative animation and philosophical depth | | **Minari** | 2020 | 2‑film Oscar nomination (Best Supporting Actress, Best Original Screenplay); 2020 Golden Globe win | • 99% Rotten Tomatoes score
• Celebrated for its authentic depiction of immigrant life | | **Tenet** | 2020 | 1‑film Oscar nomination (Best Visual Effects) | • 70% Rotten Tomatoes score
• Noted for its ambitious narrative structure and visual spectacle | | **The Father** | 2020 | 2‑film Oscar nomination (Best Actor, Best Adapted Screenplay) | • 94% Rotten Tomatoes score
• Praised for its unconventional storytelling and Anthony Hopkins’ performance | ### How to Choose Your “Best” Movie 1. **Define Your Criteria** - *Critical acclaim*: Look at Rotten Tomatoes or Metacritic scores. - *Audience reception*: Check IMDb ratings or audience reviews. - *Awards*: Consider Oscar, Golden Globe, BAFTA, or festival honors. - *Personal preference*: Genre, themes, or director’s style. 2. **Explore Multiple Sources** - *Film festivals*: Cannes, Toronto, Sundance selections. - *Industry lists*: Variety, The Hollywood Reporter, IndieWire year‑end roundups. - *Audience polls*: IMDb Top 250, Letterboxd “Most Loved” lists. 3. **Watch a Sample** - Many streaming platforms offer trailers or short clips. - If you’re undecided, start with a film that aligns with your preferred genre. ### Bottom Line While there isn’t a single definitive “best” movie of 2020, **Nomadland** is often cited as the most celebrated film of that year due to its sweeping critical praise, audience approval, and major award wins. Other contenders—such as *The Trial of the Chicago 7*, *Soul*, and *Minari*—also achieved significant acclaim and are worth watching if you’re looking for a standout 2020 experience.
